root.label: noexcept
root.note: A no-throw promise in the type system, read at compile time and enforced by std::terminate.

children.label: Specifier
children.note: noexcept or noexcept(true) is non-throwing; noexcept(false) or nothing is potentially throwing.

children.label: Constant bool argument
children.note: The argument is a constant expression and may depend on template parameters.

children.label: Conditional idiom
children.note: noexcept(noexcept(expr)): the outer is the specifier, the inner is the operator.

children.label: Not checked statically
children.note: Calling throwing code from a noexcept function is well-formed; compilers only warn.

children.label: Operator
children.note: noexcept(expr) is an unevaluated bool constant: false if expr is potentially throwing.

children.label: Unevaluated
children.note: Like sizeof, the operand never runs, so side effects never happen.

children.label: Hidden calls count
children.note: Temporaries' destructors, conversions and operator new all make the result false.

children.label: Traits
children.note: is_nothrow_move_constructible and friends are built on the operator.

children.label: Violation
children.note: An exception reaching a noexcept boundary calls std::terminate.

children.label: Unwinding unspecified
children.note: Implementation-defined whether the stack is unwound fully, partially or not at all.

children.label: Inner handlers work
children.note: Only exceptions that would cross the noexcept boundary terminate.

children.label: Implicit noexcept
children.note: Some functions get a non-throwing specification without the keyword.

children.label: Destructors
children.note: Non-throwing unless a base or member destructor is potentially throwing.

children.label: Defaulted specials
children.note: Non-throwing exactly when every function they would call is non-throwing.

children.label: C++20 explicit default
children.note: A written specifier on a defaulted function now wins; before, a mismatch deleted it.

children.label: Type system (C++17)
children.note: The exception specification is part of the function type.

children.label: One-way conversion
children.note: Pointers to noexcept functions convert to plain pointers, never the reverse.

children.label: No overloading
children.note: f() and f() noexcept conflict as redeclarations; they cannot overload.

children.label: Virtual overrides
children.note: An overrider of a noexcept virtual must be noexcept; adding noexcept is fine.

children.label: Deducible
children.note: Templates can deduce B from void(*)() noexcept(B).

children.label: Why it matters
children.note: Libraries choose algorithms based on the answer.

children.label: move_if_noexcept
children.note: vector reallocation copies copyable elements whose move may throw.

children.label: Dynamic specs removed
children.note: throw(T) removed in C++17, throw() removed in C++20.

children.label: Narrow contracts
children.note: The standard leaves functions with preconditions potentially throwing; vendors may add noexcept.
